walls.name: 230 mm Solid Brick
walls.description: Standard Delhi/North India construction: single-leaf 230 mm (9 inch) solid brick wall

walls.name: 240 mm Cavity Wall (50 mm air gap)
walls.description: Cavity wall: 115 mm outer + 50 mm air gap + 75 mm inner, improves insulation
walls.source: ECBC 2017 cavity wall with 50mm air layer (R = 0.16)

walls.name: Rat-Trap Bond Wall (230 mm)
walls.description: Laurie Baker technique: bricks laid with continuous air voids inside
walls.source: Raju et al. (2009), ECO-Niwas 2018 low-cost insulation

walls.name: 200 mm Stone Masonry
walls.description: Thick traditional stone (common in Jaipur, Jodhpur, heritage structures)
walls.source: ECBC 2017 Annex B: thermal mass, high decrement

walls.name: 200 mm RCC (Concrete)
walls.source: ECBC 2017: RCC density ~2300 kg/m³, high conductivity

walls.name: 300 mm Adobe / Rammed Earth
walls.description: High thermal mass, low conductivity; used in vernacular construction
walls.source: Minke (2006) Building with Earth; ECO-Niwas 2018 traditional materials

roofs.name: 100 mm RCC Slab (bare)
roofs.description: Exposed RCC roof slab, minimal insulation
roofs.source: ECBC 2017 Section 4.2.2.1; surface absorbance dark concrete ~0.75

roofs.name: 100 mm RCC + 20 mm Lime Plaster (whitewash)
roofs.description: RCC with white lime wash, high albedo

roofs.name: Green Roof: 80 mm RCC + 100 mm soil + plants
roofs.description: Shallow green roof with growing medium

roofs.name: 100 mm Clay Tile Barrel Vault (Mughal style)
roofs.description: Traditional barrel vault with 100 mm clay tiles, excellent thermal mass

glazing.name: Single Clear Glass (6 mm)
glazing.description: Standard single-pane clear glazing, no thermal resistance, high solar gain

glazing.name: Double Clear Glass (6–9–6 mm, air gap)
glazing.description: Double-pane clear with 9 mm air gap, better insulation

glazing.name: Tinted Bronze Glass (6 mm, single)
glazing.description: Tinted glazing reduces solar gain, common in Indian office buildings
glazing.source: ECBC 2017; tinted absorbing glass reduces SHGC by ~35%

glazing.name: Low-E Reflective Double Pane (6–9–6 mm)
glazing.description: Reflective/low-emissivity coating reduces heat transfer and solar gain
glazing.source: ECBC 2017 high-performance glazing; typical low-E coating

exterior_surface_resistance.source: ECBC 2017 Appendix A: convection & radiation resistance
